newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee hits four-month high against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee hits four-month high against dollar.

text.p: The Indian rupee hit a four-month high against the dollar on Thursday, breaching the 35.80 per dollar mark, while the central bank stood back and watched, foreign exchange dealers said.
They attributed the rupee's gain partly to a statement by Reserve Bank of India (RBI) governor on Tuesday that the central bank was allowing the market to determine the exchange rate.
The rupee traded a 35.792/800 on Thursday, compared with Tuesday's close of 35.81/82. The market was closed on Wednesday for a Hindu festival.

The rupee's latest surge came as the 15 member United Front alliance said it would choose a replacement on Friday for caretaker Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda, who was defeated by confidence vote in Parliament last week Friday.
The rival Congress party has said it will support another minority UF-led coalition if Deve Gowda is replaced.

Dealers said the political situation has had little influence on a market dominated by the central bank, and RBI governor Chakravarty Rangarajan's comments to Reuters Television on Tuesday had opened the gate for the rupee to appreciate.
"There are a number of considerations. We are now allowing the market to determine the rupee," Rangarajan said after briefing bank chief executives on the 1997/98 first half credit policy.
"The rupee was hovering at 35.820/825 (on Tuesday)," said a bank treasurer. "When the governor's statement hit the screen, the rupee immediately moved up to 35.80/81."
Dealers said RBI intervention had stopped the rupee breaking above the 35.82/83 level earlier this year. The central bank has been buying dollars throughout this year to arrest the rupee's rise.
"The whole market was long on dollars (on Tuesday), thinking RBI would buy at 35.83," a dealer said.
RBI bought dollars later on Tuesday at 35.81 level, he said.
"Inter-bank speculators and those who had built (long dollar) positions have cut-off," said another dealer.
The diminishing uncertainties on the political horizon meant continued surge of dollar inflows, analysts said.
"The rupee would continue to probe higher levels unless the market gets a signal to the contrary," another dealer said.
The rupee's fresh gain has upset exporters who have been complaining that the strong rupee has been hurting India's export competitiveness in the global market.
"We want the RBI to adjust the exchange rate as our neighbours have been doing," Ramu Deora, chairman of the Federation of Indian Export Organisations (FIEO) said.
Deora said agricultural and commodity exports were hit by the rupee's rise against the dollar at a time when the dollar had risen against major global currencies.
"In chemicals and bulk drugs, China, our major rivals, have cut prices by eight to 10 percent," Deora said.

According to the commerce ministry, Indian merchandise exports from April 1996 to January 1997 totalled $27.07 billion, up 6.19 percent from $25.49 billion over the same 10-month period from April 1995 to January 1996.
In 1995/96 (April-March), exports were valued at $31.83 billion, recording a 21.38 percent rise over the year-ago.
Indian government has been concerned about the slowdown in export growth but has blamed it largely on a downtrend in global commodity markets.
